statement: The first line holds n; the second holds n integers in any order, duplicates allowed. Print the length of the longest run of consecutive values present - the values need to exist somewhere in the array, their positions are irrelevant. Pour everything into a hash set, then count upward only from run-starts: a value whose predecessor is absent from the set. Each run is then walked exactly once, keeping the whole scan linear despite the nested while.
constraints: Values fit in 32 bits; duplicates allowed.

example.why: The values 1, 2, 3, 4 all exist - a run of four, beating the trio 100, 101, 102.

hint: One membership question filters the starts: is value minus 1 in the set?
mistake: Counting upward from every value - a single long run then gets rewalked from each member, quadratic.
